name: 3D Diorama
visualIdentity: A complete miniature stage with clear boundaries and consistent scale across buildings, characters, and props. Use an elevated or oblique view, environmental detail, and restrained depth of field; keep important models and paths sharp. The source explicitly names a 3D diorama.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to miniature sets and isometric scenes with constrained movement. It can support story worlds, seasonal campaigns, explainers, product or campus ecosystems, and process tours. Interactive HTML can add focusable callouts or object selection; that suitability is inferred from the suggested combinations and tools.
limitations: Camera tilt can break strict isometric projection; movement can expose incomplete layers or break ground contact. Excess depth separation can harm readability. Use orbit or dolly only with suitable 3D geometry or sufficient turntable views; a flat image cannot reveal unseen sides. Exploded reveals require meaningful separable components. These constraints follow from the source guidance.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Resolve colors from task, brand, or reference first; preserve exact values, semantic roles, and asset colors. The optional four-color example is background #EEE6D4, foreground #35433C, accent #7B9173, accent #B3885F; it is not intrinsic to the style. Keep accents subordinate, use discrete colors (no proposed gradient), and recheck actual composited text contrast. Example foreground text on accent 1 or 2 misses the normal-text target; place body text on a suitable existing backing rather than recoloring.
motionAndInteraction: Animate small local actions and keep state deterministic from composition time for video. Preserve projection, contact, occlusion, and reading layers. Suitable options include bounded depth parallax, purposeful chapter/story progress, or camera paths when geometry supports them. Interactive HTML may use pointer raycasting, bounded camera controls, or scroll progress with reverseable states; provide keyboard/touch and reduced-motion alternatives where relevant. Do not require live input in video.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required layer is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices, keep speech clear, and synchronize and mix with the picture. Do not assume audio assets are available.
assetRequirements: Create or source coherent 3D models, materials, lighting, and camera setup; Blender with bpy is the prescribed modeling route, with Cycles or EEVEE selected for fidelity or speed. Optional browser glTF assembly needs inspected nodes, pivots, dimensions, materials, and any animation clips. Toon ramps, outlines, soft material detail, and video-textured screens are optional treatments, not defaults. Use authorized assets; filenames do not prove licensing or animation support.
combinations: Works alone when the miniature set is the subject. Style-078 matte clay-like figures can inhabit it if palette, scale, lighting, and contact shadows stay consistent; avoid glossy/matte clashes, oversized figures, or calling it stop-motion. Style-024 handwritten arrows and callouts can guide a tour if anchored to projected positions, use existing ink/accent colors, and leave models visible. Other hybrids must preserve materials, projection, and legibility.
productionApproach: Separate responsibilities: the style renderer owns geometry, materials, lighting, and scene visuals; the motion engine owns trajectories and transforms; the composition pipeline owns timing, media/audio synchronization, checks, and export. HyperFrames is primary; Remotion is only a documented fallback for unavailability or a verified capability gap. Drive video state from seekable time; live pointer/scroll behavior is for HTML. No specific audio assets or production inputs are supplied.
